main_text.l: cturam & usus explicandos Anatomice priuatim sibi
Quatenus vero procreatur Homo, non Medico,
sed Philosopho subijcitur: nosq; eadem physica, non
Ideoq; ubi Philosophus Naturalis definit, ibi Me-
& nunc & primum quoq; quæsita & inuenta fuerit,
Pathologia summè necessaria exstitit. Hippocrat. lib.

l.i: de veteri medicina: Galen. de artis constit.

main_text.l: Affectus vox tria præter naturam, Morbum, Cau-
Sæpe tamen pro Morbis habentur, quæ tantum-
Morbus enim est διάθεσις præter naturā, à qua pri-
mum læditur actio. 2. de facult. natural. 1. de san. tuend.
Morborum etiam proprie dictorum tria summa
genera non immerito constituuntur, Similares, Or-
Omnis quoq; Morbus Vicus λόγῳ Hippocrati,
recte ἐπιλέγει[?] τινὰ ἔχει. Libro de Fract. 3.

page.notes: Top numeral read as XXIIX. with possible colon. Greek in XXXVI is partly unclear; the middle word is marked [?]. The first letter of διάθεσις is a stylised initial; it is transcribed as printed. Printed long s in "diffecandarum", "fibi", "fumme", "exiftit" and "neceffaria" is given as plain s. "facut" in the citation for XXXIV is probably "facult." and is marked as uncertain. No page number or running head is printed.
